title: Fall mornings are getting darker, and early risers notice first
dek: The sun is coming up later each week now, and people who start their day at 4 a.m. feel the change before anyone else.
body: If you are up at four, you already know it is dark out there. This time of year, it stays dark for a while longer each week. Summer mornings that used to brighten early are giving way to fall mornings that take their time.
Early risers notice this change first. Bakers, delivery drivers, parents with long commutes and people who simply like a quiet start to the day are all getting ready in the dark more often now.

For many people, the darkness itself is not the hardest part. The harder part is waking up expecting light and not getting it. Turning on a warm lamp as soon as you get up can feel gentler than stumbling around with only a phone screen.

Stepping outside for a minute once the sky starts to lighten can help too. Even a few breaths of morning air on a porch or front step can make it feel like the day has actually begun. If dark mornings leave you feeling low or worn out for weeks at a time, it is worth bringing up with a doctor.
If you are up early this week, turn on one warm light right away, and when the sun finally comes up, go stand in it for a moment.
